title: Karnataka Cabinet Expansion Triggers Congress Revolt as MLAs Demand Ministerial Berths
excerpt: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar faces open dissent from within his own party, with senior leaders resigning over portfolio allocation and more than 30 MLAs lobbying Delhi for cabinet positions.
body:
• Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar faces internal revolt within Congress as dissatisfied MLAs demand cabinet berths following the delayed second phase of cabinet expansion
  • Senior leader Ramalinga Reddy resigned from the cabinet over portfolio allocation, though the situation was later defused after intervention by party leadership
  • Multiple groups of Congress MLAs have traveled to Delhi to lobby the high command, with senior and multi-term legislators demanding at least 20 new faces in the cabinet
  • The crisis comes barely weeks after Shivakumar replaced Siddaramaiah as chief minister, exposing deep factional rifts within the Karnataka Congress

Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar is confronting his first major political crisis — not from the opposition benches, but from within his own party. Multiple Congress MLAs have publicly voiced their displeasure over cabinet formation and portfolio allocation, with at least two legislators threatening to quit and others openly demanding a reshuffle barely weeks into his tenure.

The revolt exposes fault lines that have been simmering within the Karnataka Congress since Shivakumar replaced Siddaramaiah as chief minister in late May, following a leadership transition orchestrated by the party's central leadership. The second phase of cabinet expansion, long promised to accommodate senior and first-time MLAs, remains pending — and patience has run out.

Portfolio Row Triggers Resignations

The most visible flashpoint came when Ramalinga Reddy, an eight-time MLA and one of the party's most senior leaders in Bengaluru, tendered his resignation from the cabinet. Reddy had expected the Greater Bengaluru Development portfolio, which he claimed was informally promised to him, but was instead allotted the Major and Medium Irrigation department in the gazette notification.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2084289718498562162

The situation was defused after Chief Minister Shivakumar intervened personally, holding discussions with Reddy on June 6. Party sources confirmed that Reddy agreed to continue as a minister following assurances from the leadership, though formal resolution of the resignation remained pending.

Other senior leaders have also expressed discontent. Food and Civil Supplies Minister KH Muniyappa raised concerns over his assigned department, while TB Jayachandra, a veteran Congress leader, is reportedly upset over not being included in the cabinet at all. Supporters of former minister Zameer Ahmad Khan have separately demanded a ministerial position for their leader.

MLAs March to Delhi

The discontent has taken an organized form. A delegation of more than 30 Congress MLAs, including senior multi-term legislators and first-time representatives, traveled to Delhi to press their case directly with the party high command. They met with Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, General Secretary KC Venugopal, and state in-charge Randeep Singh Surjewala.

"Surjewala told us that the cabinet will be reshuffled after 2.5 years. It has already been three years. Our demand is to make us ministers for at least the remaining two years."

— Ashok Pattan, Congress MLA

MLA AR Krishnamurthy stated that legislators who had won three, four, or even five terms were collectively pushing for new inductions. "We brought this to the notice of the Chief Minister too," he told ANI. The MLAs have demanded that at least 20 new faces be inducted into the cabinet, arguing that the current ministers have held power long enough.

Balancing Act for Shivakumar

The crisis presents a difficult balancing act for Shivakumar, who must manage competing demands across regional, caste, and seniority lines. The Karnataka cabinet has a constitutional limit of 34 ministers, and with 32 positions previously filled and two vacancies created by earlier resignations, the scope for expansion is limited.

The Congress high command issued a stern warning to MLAs, religious leaders, and community representatives against lobbying for ministerial posts, asking them to exercise patience. Despite this, delegations from various community groups and religious institutions have continued to press for cabinet berths for their preferred candidates.

Deputy Chief Minister-era dynamics continue to complicate matters. The leadership transition from Siddaramaiah to Shivakumar was framed as a strategic move to strengthen the party's Vokkaliga base ahead of future elections, but Siddaramaiah's loyalists and the broader AHINDA (Minorities, Backward Classes, Dalits) coalition feel sidelined.

What's Next

Shivakumar and Siddaramaiah are expected to meet the Congress high command in Delhi for further discussions on cabinet expansion. A final decision on new inductions is likely to follow those consultations, with the oath ceremony to be held in Bengaluru. The party is aiming to balance regional and social representation while preventing further defections — a task made harder by the approaching Greater Bengaluru Authority elections, where internal unity will be essential.
nri_angle: The internal turmoil within Karnataka's Congress government highlights the complex caste and regional dynamics that shape Indian state politics.
